value: One of the four grapes of Cotnari's traditional white blend, it is also bottled on its own, often semi sweet, and may be used for sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV DOC Cotnari specification: traditional assortment only from Grasă de Cotnari, Fetească albă, Tămâioasă românească and Frâncuşă; Fetească albă listed for sparkling and petiant wines | RomaniaTourism (Romanian National Tourist Office site): Cotnari winery's popular wines include Fetească Albă (semi sweet)

value: At Cotnari it is often left semi sweet, keeping the fresh scent of ripe grapes and vine blossom in balance with its sugar.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: smell of well ripened grape and flowering vine, excellent balance of sugars, alcohol and acidity | RomaniaTourism: Cotnari Fetească Albă semi sweet, appreciated for preserving the flavour and freshness of the grape

value: One of the four grapes of Cotnari's traditional white blend, it is also made on its own as one of the region's few dry wines, still or sparkling.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: part of the traditional four grape assortment; allowed only at full maturity (C.M.D.) and for sparkling and petiant wines | RomaniaTourism: Cotnari winery's Frâncuşă (dry) | Vincarta: Cotnari produces few dry wines, Frâncușă being one of them

value: At Cotnari it gives a crisp, lively dry white with high acidity and fresh floral and ripe grape aromas.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: smell of well ripened grape with strong floral notes; taste acid, full of freshness and fruit | RomaniaTourism: soft, dry wine, crisp and lively | Vincarta: youthful aromas of peach, grape and flowers, bitter almond on the palate

value: One of the four grapes of Cotnari's traditional white blend and the one most often bottled on its own as a sweet wine, from late picked grapes and, in some autumns, grapes touched by noble rot.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: part of the traditional four grape assortment; allowed for late harvest (C.T.) and noble rot (C.I.B.) wines; great sweet wines from noble rot in long dry autumns | Vincarta: most notable grape, capable of outstanding sweet wines occasionally affected by noble rot | RomaniaTourism: sweet whites from late harvested grapes with botrytis, such as Grasă de Cotnari

value: At Cotnari it gives sweet golden wines with honeycomb and nutty notes that turn amber and grow more complex with long bottle age.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: greenish yellow when young to straw yellow with amber tints when old; raisins, apricot, honeycomb, walnut kernel and bitter almond; sweet | RomaniaTourism: sweet, golden Grasă de Cotnari with a nutlike savour | Vincarta: honey and honeycomb notes, best aromas after 20 to 25 years in bottle

value: One of the four grapes of Cotnari's traditional white blend, it is also bottled on its own, mostly sweet from late picked or noble rot grapes, and as an aromatic sparkling wine.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Tămâioasă românească part of the traditional assortment; allowed for C.T. and C.I.B. wines and for aromatic quality sparkling wine | Vincarta: Tămâioasă among the indigenous grapes grown at Cotnari, made with skin maceration | RomaniaTourism: Tămâioasă among Cotnari winery's sweet white wines

value: A favoured red grape in Dealu Mare, permitted for its DOC still red and rosé wines.
source_notes: ONVPV DOC Dealu Mare specification: Cabernet Sauvignon in the list of red and rosé varieties | Falstaff: Dealu Mare, where Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir and Merlot are preferably cultivated | Gilbert & Gaillard: Cabernet Sauvignon among authorised varieties

value: In Dealu Mare it gives full bodied wines whose tannins are rounder and better integrated than its usual firm grip, above all on the iron rich red clays of the western hills.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: iron rich reddish brown soils of the west give body and well integrated tannins, notably in Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Fetească neagră and Syrah | Gilbert & Gaillard: reds from the iron rich soils of Valea Călugărească and Urlați show finesse and supple tannins (text closely follows the specification)

value: Permitted for DOC Dealu Mare white wines and as a base for its sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Chardonnay in white, quality sparkling and petiant variety lists | Gilbert & Gaillard: Dealu Mare Chardonnay among the awarded appellation wines

value: Permitted for DOC Dealu Mare white wines and as a base for its sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Fetească albă in white, quality sparkling and petiant variety lists | Gilbert & Gaillard: fetească albă among the authorised varieties

value: Permitted for DOC Dealu Mare red and rosé wines and for its semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Fetească neagră in red and rosé list and in petiant red list | Gilbert & Gaillard: fetească neagră among authorised varieties; red wines are the appellation's signature

value: In Dealu Mare it gives supple, vividly coloured reds on the iron rich clays around Valea Călugărească and Urlați, and more powerful, deeper coloured wines in the sunnier centres of Ceptura, Tohani and Merei.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: reds from Valea Călugărească and Urlați on iron rich reddish brown soils have light tannins and vivid colour; those of Ceptura, Tohani and Merei are more robust with more colour thanks to more heat and sun | Gilbert & Gaillard: same contrast for the appellation's reds (text closely follows the specification); fetească neagră listed

value: Permitted for DOC Dealu Mare white wines and as a base for its sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Fetească regală in white, quality sparkling and petiant variety lists | Gilbert & Gaillard: fetească regală among the authorised varieties

value: A favoured red grape in Dealu Mare, permitted for its DOC still red and rosé wines and for its sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Merlot in red and rosé list and in sparkling and petiant red lists | Falstaff: Merlot preferably cultivated in Dealu Mare | Gilbert & Gaillard: merlot among authorised varieties

value: Permitted for DOC Dealu Mare whites from dry to noble rot sweet and for its aromatic sparkling wines, which may add the name Valea Călugărească, Urlați or Tohani.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Tămâioasă românească in white list with C.I.B. yields, in aromatic sparkling list, subzone names allowed for aromatic sparkling wines | Gilbert & Gaillard: tămâioasă românească among authorised varieties

value: Permitted for DOC Dealu Mare whites from dry to noble rot sweet and for its aromatic sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Muscat Ottonel in white list with C.I.B. yields, in aromatic sparkling and petiant lists | Gilbert & Gaillard: muscat ottonel among authorised varieties

value: A favoured red grape in Dealu Mare, permitted for its DOC still red and rosé wines and for its sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Pinot noir in red and rosé list and in sparkling and petiant red lists | Falstaff: Pinot Noir preferably cultivated in Dealu Mare | Gilbert & Gaillard: pinot noir among authorised varieties

value: Permitted for DOC Dealu Mare white wines and as a base for its sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Sauvignon in white, quality sparkling and petiant variety lists | Gilbert & Gaillard: Dealu Mare Sauvignon Blanc among the awarded appellation wines

value: One of the reds Murfatlar is best known for, permitted for its dry and late harvest DOC red wines.
source_notes: ONVPV DOC Murfatlar specification: Cabernet Sauvignon allowed at full maturity (C.M.D.) and late harvest (C.T.) | RomaniaTourism: soft, rich reds, Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinot Noir the most popular | Veritas Distributors (importer) profile: dry reds from Cabernet Sauvignon

value: In Murfatlar's sunny climate it gives soft, rich reds with ripe blackberry and blueberry fruit and gentler tannins than usual.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: strong aroma of blueberries and blackberries with chocolate notes from soft tannins, without roughness; reds have velvety tannins | RomaniaTourism: soft, rich red wines, Cabernet Sauvignon among the most popular

value: Permitted for DOC Murfatlar whites from dry to late harvest and noble rot sweet, and for its ice wine and sparkling wines; the region is known for sweet late harvest versions.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Chardonnay allowed for C.M.D., C.T. and C.I.B., ice wine and sparkling | RomaniaTourism: area ideal for sweet dessert wines such as late harvest Chardonnay | Veritas profile: famous for sweet wines from late hanging grapes

value: In Murfatlar's sunny, dry climate on limestone it ripens to round, velvety and rich whites, far from the lean style of cool regions.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: velvety yet rich Chardonnay; limestone soil and long sunshine give it the best conditions in Romania | RomaniaTourism: over 300 days of sunshine, ideal for sweet late harvest Chardonnay

value: Permitted for DOC Murfatlar dry and late harvest reds and for its sparkling and semi sparkling wines.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Fetească neagră allowed at C.M.D. and C.T., in sparkling and petiant red lists | Veritas profile: the area produces dry red wines from the local Feteasca Negra

value: Permitted for DOC Murfatlar whites from dry to late harvest and noble rot sweet, and for its ice wine and aromatic sparkling wines; the region is known for sweet late harvest versions.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Muscat Ottonel allowed for C.M.D., C.T. and C.I.B., ice wine, aromatic sparkling | RomaniaTourism: sweet dessert wines such as late harvest Muscat Ottonel | Veritas profile: whites from Muscat Ottonel; famous for sweet late harvest wines

value: Permitted for DOC Murfatlar whites from dry to late harvest and noble rot sweet, and for ice wine, sparkling wine and a rosé style from its coloured skins; the region is known for sweet late harvest versions.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: Pinot Gris allowed for C.M.D., C.T. and C.I.B., ice wine, sparkling; still white or rosé from its coloured skins | RomaniaTourism: sweet dessert wines such as late harvest Pinot Gris | Veritas profile: whites from Pinot Gris; famous for sweet late harvest wines

value: In Murfatlar it builds up a lot of sugar and gives full, round and velvety wines, often made sweet from late picked grapes.
source_notes: ONVPV specification: great capacity to accumulate sugar; wines full and rich yet round and velvety | RomaniaTourism: sweet dessert wines such as late harvest Pinot Gris

value: One of the main red grapes of PGI Codru, a region better known for its whites, and the rules allow it for red, rosé and sparkling wines.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova (ONVV) Codru page: Merlot among predominant varieties, white grapes cover most of the area; winetourism.com Codru: main grapes include Merlot, white varieties dominate; Codru specification (Ministry of Agriculture order 215/2011) section 6: Merlot permitted for red, rosé and sparkling wines.

value: One of the main white grapes of PGI Codru, a region known above all for fresh white and sparkling wines, and the rules allow it for both.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova (ONVV) Codru page: Sauvignon Blanc among predominant varieties; winetourism.com Codru: main grapes include Sauvignon Blanc, known for fresh white and sparkling wines; Codru specification section 6: Sauvignon permitted for white and sparkling wines.

value: Under its Moldovan name it is a typical grape of PGI Ștefan Vodă, where its best known wines come from around Purcari, made on its own and blended with Cabernet Sauvignon and Saperavi in Negru de Purcari.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova local varieties page: best Rară Neagră wines from Purcari, Răscăieți, Leuntea, Talmaza, Căușeni, all in the Ștefan Vodă PGI; winetourism.com Moldova: typical Ștefan Vodă wines from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Saperavi and local Rară Neagră (Băbească Neagră); Ștefan Vodă specification (order 188/2011) table 1: Rara Neagră as a varietal wine name; Wine Anorak (Jamie Goode): Purcari Rară Neagră varietal and Negru de Purcari blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Saperavi, Rară Neagră; Decanter review: Negru de Purcari, Stefan Voda, Cabernet Sauvignon, Rara Neagra, Saperavi.

value: One of the typical grapes of PGI Ștefan Vodă, a region given mainly to red wine, where it is made on its own and leads blends such as Negru de Purcari with Saperavi and Rară Neagră.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova Ștefan Vodă page: Cabernet Sauvignon predominant, region known for reds; winetourism.com: an absolute red wine region, typical wines from Cabernet Sauvignon among others; Wine Anorak: Negru de Purcari blends Cabernet Sauvignon, Saperavi and Rară Neagră; Decanter review lists the same grapes for Negru de Purcari, Stefan Voda.

value: Grown for still white wines in PGI Ștefan Vodă, a region known above all for its reds.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova Ștefan Vodă page: Chardonnay among predominant varieties, region known for its reds; winetourism.com: absolute red wine region, vineyards also grow Chardonnay; Ștefan Vodă specification: Chardonnay among permitted white varieties.

value: One of the typical grapes of PGI Ștefan Vodă, a region given mainly to red wine, and the rules allow it as a varietal red and rosé.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova Ștefan Vodă page: Merlot predominant, region known for reds; winetourism.com: typical wines made from Merlot among others; Ștefan Vodă specification table 1: Merlot as varietal name for red and rosé wines.

value: One of the main grapes of PGI Valul lui Traian, a region in the south west of Moldova given mainly to red wine.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova Valul lui Traian page: Cabernet Sauvignon predominant, black varieties cover most of the area, region suits Cabernet Sauvignon; winetourism.com: red focused, much Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Fetească Neagră grown here, south western border with Romania.

value: One of the main grapes of PGI Valul lui Traian, a region in the south west of Moldova given mainly to red wine.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova Valul lui Traian page: Merlot predominant, black varieties cover most of the area; winetourism.com: much Merlot grown here, region red focused.

value: One of the red grapes the region suits best, grown here alongside Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon.
source_notes: Wine of Moldova Valul lui Traian page: region more favourable for black varieties Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Saperavi and Fetească Neagră; winetourism.com: much Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Feteasca Neagra grown here.

value: One of the only two grapes allowed in Commandaria; its bunches are dried in the sun with those of Mavro before fermentation.
source_notes: eAmbrosia PDO-CY-A1622-AM01 single document (Cyprus, Greek): main varieties Xinisteri and Ntopio Mavro only, grapes sun dried about two weeks, minimum harvest sugar set for Xynisteri. GuildSomm (Demetri Walters): Commandaria made from local Xynisteri and Mavro dried under the Cypriot sun, sugar of both must pass a threshold.

value: One of the only two grapes allowed in Commandaria; its bunches are dried in the sun with those of Xynisteri before fermentation.
source_notes: eAmbrosia PDO-CY-A1622-AM01: main varieties Ntopio Mavro and Xinisteri only, sun dried about two weeks; Mavro must reach a higher harvest sugar (258 g/l) than Xynisteri (212 g/l). GuildSomm: Commandaria made from local Xynisteri and Mavro dried under the sun.

value: The white grape of the PDO: dry whites must be at least 85 percent Xynisteri, with permitted local and some international grapes making up the rest.
source_notes: GuildSomm: outside Commandaria, PDO dry whites must contain at least 85% Xynisteri; for Pitsilia and Krasochoria Lemesou specific international varieties can also be included. Wines of Cyprus (winesofcyprus.co.uk, dated 2011): Wine Villages of Limassol use the Pitsilia rules, Xynisteri at least 85%.

value: A red PDO wine here can be at least 85 percent Maratheftiko, the other grape allowed to lead in that way being Ofthalmo, with permitted local and international grapes making up the rest.
source_notes: GuildSomm: first red PDO style requires at least 85% Maratheftiko or Ofthalmo, remainder permitted native and international varieties. Wines of Cyprus (2011): Wine Villages of Limassol reds Maratheftiko or Ofthalmo at least 85%.

value: Red PDO wines may also be built on Mavro, which must then make up at least 60 percent of the blend, the rest coming from permitted local and international grapes.
source_notes: GuildSomm: second red PDO style uses a minimum of 60% Mavro with permitted native and international varieties. Wines of Cyprus (2011): Wine Villages of Limassol reds may be 60% Mavro with 30% of one specified foreign variety.

value: One of the international grapes allowed in this PDO, where it can complete a red blend led by Maratheftiko, Ofthalmo or Mavro.
source_notes: Open Wine Map, reproducing the eAmbrosia entry PDO-CY-A1628: lists Cabernet-Sauvignon N among the PDO grape varieties. GuildSomm: Krasochoria Lemesou may include specific international varieties; red PDO wines are led by at least 85% Maratheftiko or Ofthalmo, or at least 60% Mavro, with permitted native and international varieties for the rest.

value: One of the international grapes allowed in this PDO, where it can complete a red blend led by Maratheftiko, Ofthalmo or Mavro.
source_notes: Open Wine Map, reproducing the eAmbrosia entry PDO-CY-A1628: lists Merlot Noir among the PDO grape varieties. GuildSomm: Krasochoria Lemesou may include specific international varieties; red PDO wines are led by at least 85% Maratheftiko or Ofthalmo, or at least 60% Mavro, with permitted native and international varieties for the rest.

value: One of the international grapes allowed in this PDO, where it can complete a red blend led by Maratheftiko, Ofthalmo or Mavro.
source_notes: Open Wine Map, reproducing the eAmbrosia entry PDO-CY-A1628: lists Shiraz among the PDO grape varieties. GuildSomm: Krasochoria Lemesou may include specific international varieties; red PDO wines are led by at least 85% Maratheftiko or Ofthalmo, or at least 60% Mavro, with permitted native and international varieties for the rest.

value: One of six grapes allowed for the red and rosé wines of PDO Sakar, grown at the foot of the Sakar mountain along the Maritsa river.
source_notes: UK register copy of the PDO Sakar specification: red and rosé varieties are Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Syrah, Mavrud and Malbec; vineyards at the foot of the Sakar mountains along the Maritsa. Wine Folly: South Sakar is an area good for Syrah and Merlot.

value: One of six grapes allowed for the red and rosé wines of PDO Sakar, grown at the foot of the Sakar mountain along the Maritsa river.
source_notes: UK register copy of the PDO Sakar specification: red and rosé varieties are Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Syrah, Mavrud and Malbec. Wine Folly: South Sakar is an area good for Syrah and Merlot.

value: A late ripening grape, it is grown here because the Struma valley is warmer than the rest of Bulgaria, and it is the parent of the earlier ripening Melnik crossings bred for the area.
source_notes: Wine Anorak (Jamie Goode): because this is a warmer region they can grow broadleaf Melnik here; its offspring were bred to be earlier ripening. Exotic Wine Travel: a late ripening variety, which is why producers made a hybrid. Wine Folly: Melnik 55 is a cross of Broad leafed Melnik and Valdiguié.

value: Bred from Shiroka Melnishka to ripen earlier, it is made here both as a single varietal wine and in blends.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Melnik 55 a cross of Broad leafed Melnik and Valdiguié; describes both blended wines and pure single varietal Early Melnik. Wine Anorak: Melnik offspring bred to be earlier ripening. Exotic Wine Travel: parent is late ripening, hence the hybrid.

value: On the volcanic soils of Santorini Assyrtiko is at its leanest and most concentrated, bone dry and crisp with a pronounced, flinty minerality.
source_notes: Wines of Greece: on Santorini it makes the lean, mineral and very concentrated PDO Santorini whites. Decanter: wines classified Santorini are bone dry, crisp, mineral laden, high acid; unoaked to keep mineral, flinty character.

value: In the warmer, drier vineyards of Drama Assyrtiko is more aromatic and rounder than on Santorini, with a more discreet minerality.
source_notes: Wines of Greece (Drama region page): in Drama Assyrtiko yields wines far more aromatic and elegant than in its birthplace. Decanter: mainland Assyrtiko is more aromatic, rounder, with a more discreet minerality.

value: Picked late on the cold Mantinia plateau, Moschofilero gives light, low alcohol whites with a lively, high acidity.
source_notes: Wines of Greece: late ripening in one of Greece's coldest zones gives low alcohol, intensely aromatic wines with light body and titillating acidity. Decanter: cool region, late harvest, light dry whites high in acidity, alcohol about 11.5 percent.

value: Naoussa gives Xinomavro at its most structured, with firm tannins and a high, almost sour acidity that need years in bottle to soften.
source_notes: GuildSomm: high, almost sour acidity and strong tannin, harsh if unmanaged, develops beautifully in bottle. Decanter: Naoussa Xinomavro has the feisty tannic and acid structure of Nebbiolo. Wines of Greece: in cold rainy years the tannic character becomes more pronounced.

value: The cold, high Amyndeon plateau gives a fresher, sharper Xinomavro than Naoussa, well suited to the rosé and sparkling wines made here.
source_notes: Wines of Greece: Florina is the coldest area of Greece; Amynteo Xinomavro has a different character from Naoussa; rosé still and sparkling wines are particularly significant. GuildSomm: Amynteo among the coldest regions, colder than Naoussa, excels in sparkling wine; acidity elevated.

value: Fermented with Negoska, Xinomavro here gives fruitier, softer and smoother reds than in Naoussa, easier to enjoy young.
source_notes: GuildSomm: Goumenissa elements combine to make more fruity and full bodied wines. Decanter: Negoska softens tannins and lightens acidity; Goumenissa has smoother, silkier fruit than Naoussa. Wines of Greece: blended with Negoska so the wines become more attractive while young.

value: In Goumenissa the dark, fruity Negoska softens Xinomavro's tannins and acidity and deepens its colour, giving rounder, tamer wines than Naoussa's.
source_notes: Wines of Greece: dark and fruity Negoska with medium acidity and tannins rounds off the blend, giving Goumenissa a rounded, chocolaty, far tamer flavour than Naoussa. Decanter: Negoska softens the tannins, lightens the acidity and boosts the colour of Xinomavro.

value: Blended with Krasato and Stavroto on the slopes of Mount Olympus, Xinomavro gives softer, riper reds here, slightly rustic and approachable younger.
source_notes: GuildSomm: Rapsani wines are a touch softer and riper than most from the other Xinomavro appellations and a tad rustic; co fermented blend of three varieties. Wines of Greece: blended with Stavroto and Krassato (Rapsani) so the wines become more attractive while young.

value: The only grape allowed in PDO Patra, made as dry, medium dry and medium sweet whites, with its best sites on the slopes of Panachaiko and in the mountain vineyards of Aigialeia.
source_notes: Wines of Greece PDO Patra: Roditis 100 percent; dry, medium dry, medium sweet white; most beautiful part is the mountain area of Egialia. Decanter: Roditis forms the backbone of the Patras appellation; best sites are the slopes of Panachaiko and Egialia.

value: In the cool mountain vineyards of Aigialeia Roditis ripens slowly into its most aromatic wines, while lower, warmer sites near Patras give fuller, more generous whites.
source_notes: Wines of Greece (Achaia): gentle ripening in Egialia yields the most aromatic Roditis; around Patras it ripens earlier, giving fuller bodied wines. Decanter: warmer Peloponnese climate gives more generous Roditis; Egialia named among best sites. Aroma claim rests mainly on Wines of Greece.

value: Blended with the softer Kotsifali in the reds of Peza and Archanes, where Archanes uses more of it, and a minor partner to Liatiko in red Sitia.
source_notes: Wines of Greece: Peza red is Kotsifali and Mandilari, its rough character needing the softer Kotsifali; Archanes has the same composition with a higher Mandilaria content; Sitia red is Liatiko at least 80 percent with Mandilaria. Wines of Crete: Mandilari is in the blend for PDO Peza and PDO Archanes.

value: Mandilari
source_notes: Wines of Greece PDO Peza: Mandilaria is called Mandilari in Crete. Wines of Crete (Cretan winemakers' network): the variety page is titled Mandilari.

value: Cretan Liatiko is pale in colour, and in Sitia and Dafnes it also makes concentrated sweet wines with notes of figs, jam and dried fruit.
source_notes: Wines of Greece: Liatiko is a pale hued cultivar suited to excellent sweet wines (Dafnes); produces excellent concentrated sweet wines in Sitia. Wines of Crete: lacking in colour but offers unique sweetness; aromas of figs, raspberry jam, dried fruits.
